correctness.rationale: Mori's Lemma 3.5 makes both \(L_\phi(u)=\sum_j u([\gamma_j])\) and \(Q_\phi(u)=\sum_j u([\gamma_j])^2\) factorization invariants. For the reference Calabi-Yau factorization both equal its length \(m\). Hence for any competing positive factorization, with integer \(x_j=u([\gamma'_j])\), one has \(\sum x_j=\sum x_j^2=m\). Therefore \(\sum x_j(x_j-1)=0\); every integer summand is nonnegative and vanishes only for 0 or 1, proving the zero-one law and exactly \(m\) ones. Mori's rank and Euler-characteristic formulas then give the asserted allowable-filling defect identities.
